_about_en: English for the vision-pass discrepancy fields that quote the patent in Chinese. output/translations.json is the verified index and is applied first, by longest match; it covers the compound names but not the surrounding prose, and substring substitution into free prose produces unreadable half-translated sentences. So each field listed here is hand-authored as a whole sentence, using the verified index's English for every compound name so the wording stays identical to the gold. Keyed by '<page>#<discrepancy index>.<field>' against input/vision/*.json, which is read-only, so these keys are stable. Chinese characters are quoted nowhere: where the patent's exact printed characters are the point of the finding, the finding is stated in English instead.

entries.p01#0.text_says: Step 5) is titled 'Synthesis of methyl 2-chloro-3-bromomethyl-4-methylsulfonylbenzoate' and step 6) is titled 'Synthesis of 2-chloro-3-(2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy)methyl-4-methylsulfonylbenzoic acid'. The two characters meaning 'methyl ester' are printed in the step 5 title and absent from the step 6 title. Which of the two is intended must be settled against the description pages, not against this page.
entries.p02#0.text_says: The text says the product concentrated out is the ETHYL ester of 2-chloro-3-(2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy)methyl-4-methylsulfonylbenzoic acid, while the only starting material charged is the METHYL ester of 2-chloro-3-bromomethyl-4-methylsulfonylbenzoic acid together with sodium 2,2,2-trifluoroethoxide. Nothing in the step could turn a methyl ester into an ethyl ester.
entries.p02#1.text_says: The text says an appropriate amount of peroxybenzoic acid is added and that bromine is then added dropwise under reflux.
entries.p02#2.text_says: The text says the 3-oxo-1-cyclohexenyl ester, cyanoacetone and triethylamine are dissolved in solvent and stirred continuously at room temperature.
entries.p02#3.text_says: The text calls the target a triketone herbicide and gives it a Chinese common name that is neither the standard Chinese name for tembotrione nor the standard Chinese name for sulcotrione. The intermediates the claims recite carry the 3-[(2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy)methyl] group, and that group is what distinguishes tembotrione from sulcotrione.
entries.p02#4.text_says: The text says a mixture of cyclohexanedione and base is added, while the product it then names is the 3-oxo-1-cyclohexenyl ester of the benzoic acid.
entries.p03#0.text_says: Every species on this page is named in prose only: 2-chloro-6-methylsulfonyltoluene, methyl 2-chloro-4-methylsulfonyl-3-methylbenzoate, methyl 2-chloro-3-bromomethyl-4-methylsulfonylbenzoate, 2-chloro-3-(2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy)methyl-4-methylsulfonylbenzoic acid, and cyclohexanedione.
entries.p03#1.text_says: Claim 3 names 2-chloro-6-methylsulfonyltoluene, putting the mesyl group at position 6. Claim 4 names methyl 2-chloro-4-methylsulfonyl-3-methylbenzoate, putting the mesyl group at position 4.
entries.p03#2.text_says: Claim 3 refers to step 2), claim 4 to step 5), claim 5 to step 6) and claim 6 to step 7).
entries.p03#3.what: The trifluoroethyl locants are printed inconsistently between claims: claim 5 names sodium trifluoroethoxide with no locants, while claim 6 writes the (2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy) form in full. Both are preserved as printed rather than normalised to one another.
entries.p03#3.text_says: Claim 5 prints sodium trifluoroethoxide without locants; claim 6 prints (2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy)methyl with locants.
entries.p03#4.text_says: Claim 3 offers dichloromethane, chloroform or 1,2-dichloroethane. Claim 4 offers carbon tetrachloride, chloroform, dichloromethane or 1,2-dichloroethane.
entries.p04#0.text_says: Every species on this page is named in prose only: 2-(2-chloro-4-methylsulfonyl-3-[(2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy)methyl]benzoyl)cyclohexane-1,3-dione as the target in [0002]; 2-chlorotoluene; 2-chloro-6-methylsulfonyltoluene; 2-chloro-3-acetyl-6-methylsulfonyltoluene; 2-chloro-3-methyl-4-methylsulfonylbenzoic acid; and methyl 2-chloro-3-methyl-4-methylsulfonylbenzoate.
entries.p04#1.text_says: [0003] lists the prior-art drawbacks as the use of sodium methanethiolate and of N-bromosuccinimide. [0004] says the invention does away with sodium methanethiolate and with highly toxic cyanoacetone.
entries.p04#2.text_says: [0002] prints the target's name with the chlorine locant and the following position number run together, with no dash between them, inside the 2-chloro-4-methylsulfonyl portion. Verified at four times magnification and recorded as printed.
entries.p04#3.what: [0002] names a comparator herbicide whose Chinese name is not a standard Chinese herbicide name, alongside a second comparator whose Chinese name is a common Chinese name for mesotrione. The characters were verified individually at six times magnification and were not corrected.
entries.p04#3.text_says: [0002] states that the activity of the target is higher than that of the two comparator herbicides currently on the market.
entries.p04#4.what: [0003] prints the brominating agent in a Chinese form that is not the standard Chinese name for N-bromosuccinimide: one character of the standard name is replaced by a different character, and another character of the standard name is missing. Verified at five times magnification and recorded as printed.
entries.p04#4.text_says: [0003] item (3) says that N-bromosuccinimide is used as the brominating agent and that this brominating agent is expensive. The name is printed in a non-standard Chinese form.
entries.p05#0.text_says: [0017] says that the METHYL ester of 2-chloro-3-bromomethyl-4-methylsulfonylbenzoic acid is dissolved in solvent, and that what is concentrated out is the ETHYL ester of 2-chloro-3-(2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy)methyl-4-methylsulfonylbenzoic acid. The character that makes the product an ethyl ester was verified at high magnification. It is almost certainly a printing error for methyl, but it is transcribed exactly as printed. The final product of [0017] and the [0016] heading are both the free acid, so the ester identity does not change the outcome of the route.
entries.p05#1.text_says: [0015] says an appropriate amount of peroxybenzoic (perbenzoic) acid is added. Verified character by character: the printed name is peroxybenzoic acid, NOT benzoyl peroxide. Recorded as printed; a downstream chemistry pass should treat the initiator's identity as flagged rather than settled.
entries.p05#2.text_says: [0021] says cyanoacetone and triethylamine. Verified character by character: the printed name is cyanoacetone, NOT acetone cyanohydrin. Recorded as printed and flagged, not corrected.
entries.p05#3.text_says: [0014] and [0015] name the compound as methyl 2-chloro-3-methyl-4-methylsulfonylbenzoate; [0024] names it as methyl 2-chloro-4-methylsulfonyl-3-methylbenzoate. Both give the same 2-chloro, 3-methyl, 4-methylsulfonyl pattern, so this is a variation in the order the substituents are cited and not a structural conflict.
entries.p05#4.text_says: [0019] and [0026] both say only 'cyclohexanedione' and never '1,3-cyclohexanedione'. The 1,3-isomer is implied by the product name '3-oxo-1-cyclohexenyl ester' but is nowhere stated, and the isomer has NOT been inferred into the transcription.
entries.p06#0.text_says: [0031] says the process uses methanesulfonyl chloride in place of the chloro-substitution reaction of the methyl sulfide.
entries.p06#1.text_says: [0031] says the process does away with the hydrogen-peroxide oxidation step of the thioether.
entries.p06#3.text_says: [0031] says bromine is used in place of expensive N-bromosuccinimide for the side-chain methyl bromination, and presents this as an improvement of the invention over the prior art.
entries.p06#6.text_says: [0035] charges 1,2-dichloroethane as the reaction solvent but names the extraction solvent '1,2-dichloromethane', which is not a real compound.
entries.p07#0.text_says: [0038] gives 34.0 g as 0.2 mol, implying a molar mass of 170.0. [0042] gives 50.88 g as 0.24 mol, implying 212.0. [0046] gives 42.8 g as 0.2 mol, implying 214.0. The molar masses of the same compounds WITHOUT their chlorine are 170.2, 212.3 and 214.2 respectively, which are exact matches. The stated yields also close exactly on that same des-chloro basis: in [0038], 36.5 g divided by 212.3 is 0.172 mol, which is 86.0 per cent against the 86 per cent printed; in [0046], 44.2 g divided by 228.3 is 0.194 mol, which is 96.8 per cent against the 97 per cent printed. Computed on the chlorinated molar masses the same yields would be 74 per cent and 84 per cent. By contrast the two non-aromatic reagents in [0038] are correct as printed (aluminium trichloride at 40.5 g for 0.3 mol implies 135 against an actual 133.3; acetyl chloride at 23.5 g for 0.3 mol implies 78.3 against an actual 78.5), so the error is confined to the chlorinated aromatic substrates.
entries.p07#1.text_says: [0042] charges 0.24 mol of substrate and reports 82 g of dried white solid at 72 per cent yield. 0.24 multiplied by 0.72 is 0.1728 mol, so 82 g would require a molar mass of 474 g/mol. A 72 per cent yield corresponds to 43.0 g on the chlorinated basis, or 37.0 g on the des-chloro basis. The figure is transcribed as printed (82 g, verified at high magnification) and no corrected value is inferred here.
entries.p08#0.text_says: The text says what is concentrated out is the ETHYL ester of 2-chloro-3-(2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy)methyl-4-methylsulfonylbenzoic acid, whereas the substrate charged is the METHYL ester of 2-chloro-3-bromomethyl-4-methylsulfonylbenzoic acid.
entries.p08#1.text_says: The text says thionyl chloride 71.4 (0.6 mol) is added dropwise. The figure 71.4 carries no unit, while 60.4 g, 0.05 g, 24.5 g and 22.2 g in the same paragraph all carry grams.
entries.p08#2.text_says: The text says only 'cyclohexanedione', with no locants given.
entries.p08#3.text_says: [0050] gives 39.6 g as 0.22 mol of bromine, implying a formula weight of 180 against 159.8 for Br2. [0057] gives 60.4 g as 0.2 mol of the benzoic acid, implying 302 against 346.7. On the same page, thionyl chloride at 71.4 for 0.6 mol, cyclohexanedione at 24.5 g for 0.22 mol and triethylamine at 22.2 g for 0.22 mol all reconcile.
entries.p09#0.text_says: The text gives 198 g as 0.5 mol of substrate, which implies a molecular weight of 396. It then reports 188 g of beige solid concentrated out at 95 per cent yield from 0.5 mol, which implies a molecular weight of 395.8 (188 divided by 0.5 times 0.95). Against the drawn molecular weight of 440.82, the true yield from 198 g would be about 85 per cent, and 188 g is 85.3 per cent of the 220.4 g theoretical. The triethylamine figure (60.6 for 0.6 mol, molecular weight 101.19) is internally correct, so the inconsistency is confined to the substrate and the product.
entries.p09#2.text_says: The text gives 0.2 g of cyanoacetone as catalyst, triethylamine at 60.6 (0.6 mol) as base, and 500 ml of acetonitrile as solvent, at room temperature for 24 hours.
